text: William S. Burroughs's Naked Lunch, first published in 1959, was banned as “hard-core pornography” by Customs after an imported copy was seized at Port Adelaide in February 1960. US Customs embargoed it as allegedly obscene under the Tariff Act (1930). In a proceeding begun by a petition filed on September 17, 1964, the Superior Court adjudged Naked Lunch obscene, but the final decree was reversed and a new decree was ordered declaring that the book could not be declared obscene. In November 1967 the Tribunal held it to be indecent in New Zealand.
